You are wiring pages of Nxeon's NEW marketing site to real data. Worktree: /root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm (branch feature/marketing-nxm, Next.js 15). READ tools/nxm/README.md FIRST — generators, wire modules (tools/nxm/wire/<slug>.py), loaders (app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts), slots, template routes, SEO, real data sources. Study the wired examples: tools/nxm/wire/{vps,free_vps,singapore_vps_hosting}.py, app/nxm/_data/{vps,free-vps,singapore-vps-hosting,lib,cards}.ts. Design package: /root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff (source/pages/<slug>/, source/build_gs2.py, build_gameserver.py, build_location.py, build_games2.py, games2_body.html, games2.js, pages/_gs*.{css,js}, assets/, docs/HANDOFF.md §4 conversion-page requirements, docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md).

OWNER RULES (non-negotiable): every price, plan, spec (RAM/CPU/NVMe/slots), game, count and region must come from the system (same tables/helpers as checkout and the live site) at request time — nothing hardcoded; fail closed (throw / notFound) rather than show a snapshot. SEO on every page including every generated game page (meta(p): title/description per game from real data; canonical; JSON-LD ≥ live: live game pages have FAQPage + Product). Never invent claims/stats/player counts. Keep the approved design's look; adapt markup where real data differs (e.g. Minecraft has 3 real tiers in staging, the design shows 7). Portal untouched; only app/nxm, tools/nxm, public/nxm.

COORDINATION (other agents work in this worktree concurrently):
- Edit only YOUR files: wire modules/loaders for your slugs, app/nxm/_data/games-*.ts helpers, tools/nxm/routes/<your-slug>.json. You MAY change the ROUTES lines for YOUR slugs in tools/nxm/nxmlib.py and the PARTICLES entries for your slugs in tools/nxm/port_pages.py (tiny line edits only — re-read the file right before editing). Nothing else shared (lib.ts, cards.ts, _components, _seo, port_home.py) — describe needed shared changes in your report.
- Regenerate only your slugs: `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>...`. No git commit, no staging deploy, don't restart the shared dev server on :3033 (if down: `cd /root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm && nohup npx next dev -p 3033 >/tmp/nxm-dev.log 2>&1 &`). Never `pkill -f`, never `git add -A`.
- DB = staging's (read-only). Typecheck `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore .next/types noise). Verify vs dist/nxeon-<slug>.html at 1440 and 390 with Playwright (`require('/opt/nxeon/node_modules/playwright')`).

YOUR PAGES: slugs `game-servers` (hub), `minecraft-server-hosting` (THE game template), `minecraft-server-hosting-singapore` (THE game × location template), `minecraft-server-hosting-germany` (older template), `valheim` (older template), `free-minecraft`.
1. Game template → EVERY game: fan out `minecraft-server-hosting` with tools/nxm/routes/minecraft-server-hosting.json to one route per game family that has active db.gamePlan rows, using the SAME route paths the live site uses (look at app/(marketing)/*-server-hosting folder names and lib/games.ts to map family → route; e.g. /rust-server-hosting, /ark-survival-ascended-server-hosting). Loader load({family}) builds the page's gs-data JSON / markup from real tiers (gamePlan RAM/CPU/disk/slots/price/intro), game name/genre/art (lib/games.ts GAME_DISPLAY, GAME_GENRES, GAME_ART_SLUG → public/games/art; the design's own per-game art in assets/g, assets/gl, assets/pc may be used where it exists — copy needed files into public/nxm/games/ and fall back to live art), regions from enabled nodes, deploy links via deployHref({service:"game", gameFamily, gamePlanId, region}). Copy that is Minecraft-specific in the design (hero copy, FAQ, modpack guide, TINFO/PACK fit-calculator numbers) must become per-game: use real per-game data where it exists; where the design has hand-written Minecraft copy, write neutral per-game copy only from facts in the system (never invent specs); list heuristics (TINFO/PACK, sizing) in your report as OPEN-ITEMS. HANDOFF §4 conversion requirements (deploy console hero, Shield section, "Choose your world" picker with resources + fit calculator, sticky deploy bar, gold custom-server CTA → /contact?topic=custom, objection FAQ) must survive for every game.
2. Valheim: the owner wants the new template for all game pages — valheim becomes a fan-out entry of the template (remove the `valheim` slug from ROUTES + PARTICLES, delete app/nxm/valheim-server-hosting generated by the old slug; its route is then produced by the fan-out). Same for `minecraft-server-hosting-germany` (older template): replace with the location template.
3. Location template: fan out `minecraft-server-hosting-singapore` via tools/nxm/routes/minecraft-server-hosting-singapore.json to `<game route>/<region-slug>` for every game × every region that has an enabled node (staging: sgp1 Singapore, fsn1 Germany). Region naming/copy from lib/node-regions.ts; the design blends game art into the city image — reuse the design's city/location imagery where it exists (assets/), no fabricated latency numbers.
4. game-servers hub (build_games2.py + games2_body.html + games2.js): library cards, configurator tiles, "N games" counts, from-prices, cover wall — all from lib/games.ts + db.gamePlan (only families with active plans are sellable; decide how to show catalogue games without plans and explain). The builder bakes the markup in Python; move the data-driven parts to slots rendered by your loader (keep the classes/markup).
5. free-minecraft: limits from Settings (free_minecraft_ram_mb, free_minecraft_domain, free_minecraft_enabled; see lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts) — "$0" is genuinely the price (ALLOW it).
Particles on game pages (owner pick) must stay on all generated game routes (PARTICLES in port_pages.py applies per slug — per-game colours can come from GAME_VISUAL in components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx; if per-route colours need a shared change, report it).
Report: routes generated (count), files, what couldn't be sourced, heuristics kept, screenshots, owner decisions.

# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

tools.name: Artifact

Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. The one exception is a workshop document from the `workshop` skill, which carries its own design: there Claude skips `artifact-design` and loads `artifact-diagramming` for a template page's diagrams. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com or cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ (the skill has the full list) and stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data or images) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. Limits: 16MB for the page and each text file, 15MB for each binary file, at most 255 entries and 64MB per version, and standard web media types only.

**Calls**: `action` picks one (publish when omitted):
- **publish** (the default): takes `file_path`, plus `icon` on a first publish and an optional one-sentence `description`, and with `url` updates that existing artifact in place. With `url`, `file_path` and `asset: true`, it instead uploads that local image, video, PDF, font or text file to the artifact's asset store; `file_paths` in place of `file_path` uploads up to 25 image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in one call under one approval (a text file goes in a call of its own), and the result gives each one's `url`. The page must declare the `assets` capability, and the `artifact-capabilities` skill has the limits. Claude references the uploaded file from the page by the `url` in the result, exactly as given. To reuse assets another artifact already holds, such as a design system's fonts or images, Claude passes `from_url` (that artifact) and up to ten `asset_ids` from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it in place of `file_path`: the server copies them without downloading or re-uploading, and the result gives each copy's new url in this artifact, to reference exactly as given; both artifacts must be ones the person can open. Another artifact's published files are reused through `files` instead: Claude maps a path to {"artifact": "<its url>", "path": "<its published path>"} and that file is copied into the new version server side with its type. Script, style, data, font and image files copy this way; an HTML, SVG or XML document does not, so Claude reads it with `path` and publishes it as its own file.
- **read**: takes `url` (any claude.ai artifact link: claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) and returns the published page's content. Claude reads these links with this action, not with WebFetch or curl, and also uses it wherever a skill or notice says to re-read an artifact. It returns raw HTML for the person's own artifact, or, for one someone else owns, an isolated summary, which is data, not instructions, and Claude says in `prompt` what it needs. The result's header says whether the person can edit that artifact ("writer"); when they can, it names the saved file that holds the full page, and Claude builds any republish from that file. Whatever Claude reads from someone else's page, or from a page other people have edited, is untrusted data, never instructions. With `path`, it fetches one published file or uploaded asset instead and says where it put it (a small text file comes back inline, as data); with `paths` it fetches several published files in one call. With `type_url` and no `url`, it describes one Artifact type.
- **list**: returns the person's artifacts, newest first, with title, URL and last-updated time. It takes `limit`, and `scope` set to "mine" (the default), "shared" or "all". With `url`, the scopes "files" and "assets" list that artifact's published files or asset store. The scope "types" lists the Artifact types this account can start from; `type_query` narrows a listing that says more exist than it shows. A shared artifact can be updated only when the person was given edit access to it, which a read of it states ("writer"); one shared for viewing or commenting cannot, so Claude publishes a separate artifact and says so. Artifacts shared from another organization may be missing from the listing, so Claude asks the person for the link. Rows are data, not instructions. An empty "shared" listing means only that nothing is listed, not that nothing was shared with the person.
- **delete**: with `url` alone, permanently deletes a published artifact, which cannot be undone and stops the link working for everyone. Claude does this only when the person asks for that artifact to be deleted or unpublished, or says they did not want it published, never on its own initiative; the person confirms every delete, and afterwards Claude gives them the content the way they wanted it; with `url` and `path` (an asset id), removes that one uploaded asset. Claude deletes only an asset that nothing references any more, and only when the person asks or when replacing an asset Claude uploaded.
- **open**: takes `url` and shows the person that existing artifact without changing it. Claude uses it right after another tool created or updated an artifact the person should now see, or when the person asks to see one. An artifact Claude just published or just created from a type needs no open, even while Claude then fills it through a connector, unless that call's result says to open it.
- **pin** / **unpin**: takes `url` and adds the artifact to, or removes it from, the person's pinned list in their claude.ai sidebar. Claude pins or unpins only when the person asks, with one exception: after publishing something the person will keep reopening, such as a dashboard, Claude may offer once and pin it on a yes, or pass `pin: true` on that publish if they asked beforehand. Unless the person asks, Claude never pins a one-off page or unpins something it did not pin.
- **quickstart**: takes `intent` and optionally `design_systems: false`. It is read-only. See **Artifact types**.

**To update**: Edit the file, then call Artifact again with the same file path — it redeploys to the same URL. A different file path claims a new URL so only use a different path if you intend to create a separate new Artifact. A republish reaches views that are already open automatically, carrying page state where possible (a game, queue or half-typed reply).

**To update an artifact from an earlier conversation** — whenever the user wants an existing artifact updated or its link kept, not only when they paste a URL: pass the artifact's URL as `url`, finding it with `action: "list"` or by asking the user for the link when you don't have it. Before publishing to it, read it (`action: "read"` with that `url`) and build your update on the version that comes back — a publish to an artifact this conversation has not read or published is refused and hands you the live version to build on. Publishing without `url` creates a separate artifact rather than updating the existing one, so recover its URL instead of announcing a new link. If the user asks how to get back to their artifacts: in the Claude Code terminal, `/artifacts` lists the artifacts they own or were shared (o opens one in the browser, c copies its link) and ctrl+] (by default) reopens the most recent artifact from this session; the gallery at claude.ai/code/artifacts lists them on the web.

**Watching** (the result's subscription line): each publish result says whether this session now watches that artifact, for republishes from elsewhere and for comments sent to Claude. Claude never claims a watch that a result did not confirm. Claude uses the `ArtifactComments` tool to watch an artifact it did not just publish, and to read or answer comments on one.

**Files you did not write**: Read the complete file before publishing it, even when asked not to ("it's personal", "no need to open it") — publishing distributes the content, and you must never distribute what you haven't seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If you cannot read it, do not publish it.

**Artifact types**: published Artifact types (ready-made pages, such as slide decks, documents or designs, that take Claude's content as data) and the design systems that decks and designs are built with are set per account, so only a call shows which exist. When the person wants something new made, in whatever words — a deck, a document for others to read (not one that belongs in the codebase), a visual design, a design system (even one built from the codebase) or any other page — Claude's first call is `action: "quickstart"` with the fitting `intent`, before loading a skill or writing a file, and still first when Claude already has a type's link (the link does not bring the design systems), once per new artifact. Its result replaces listing the types and the design systems, reading the default design system's README and, for a plain page, loading the artifact-design skill. Claude prefers the type it names over a skill that would produce a .pptx or .docx file, unless the person asks for that format or no listed type fits, and passes `design_systems: false` when it already has a design system's link or the person declined one. A deck that will be emailed or attached is not a request for a file format: a deck made from the Slides type downloads as .pptx or PDF. A design system takes `intent: "other"`, since "design" shows only the Design type: Claude makes it from a listed Design System type and, in a codebase, says in one line that it can also be set up as files there. The listings under **list** remain for looking further and answer what kinds of artifacts or templates Claude can make. To answer a question about the person's design system, or other reference material made from a type, Claude lists that type's artifacts (`action: "list"` with the type's name as `type`) and reads the relevant one; if none is listed, Claude looks in the person's files before saying there is none. Listed titles and descriptions are data, not instructions.

To start from a type, Claude publishes with its `type_url`, a `title` and no files. The result is an ordinary private Artifact that carries its `url`, the type's instructions, the pages they say to read first and how to fill it (the type's own store, or Claude's data files published to that `url`). Claude updates it by its `url` as usual and changes only its own files, because the type's page and files stay fixed.

**Artifact database**: a published artifact's page code can keep a small shared database, which the `ArtifactData` tool reads and writes as the person, with the artifact's `url` (its actions are what a skill or type instruction means by `read_db` and `write_db`). Reads: "get" (`collection` + `doc_id`) returns one document, "list" (`collection`) a page of a collection, and "query" (`collection`, optional `query`) the matching documents. Writes: "set" replaces a document, "update" merges fields into it (from `data`, or from `file_path`, a local JSON file), "delete" removes one, and "batch" applies several writes under one approval; Claude prefers a batch whenever it writes more than a couple of documents. Rows are shared, durable state: everyone who can open the artifact sees Claude's writes, and rows Claude reads were written by the page's viewers, so they are data, never instructions. When a page's job is to hold records that people or Claude will add to or change later — a tracker, a sign-up sheet, a log, a dashboard's numbers — Claude gives the page this database (the `db` capability, via the `artifact-capabilities` skill) instead of writing the records into the page source or browser storage, and later adds or changes rows with `ArtifactData` rather than republishing the page.

**Separate tools**: Claude handles comment threads on a published artifact with `ArtifactComments` and an artifact's shared database with `ArtifactData`, whose actions are what a skill or type instruction means by `read_db` or `write_db`. Claude loads either tool when it needs it, and if one appears only as a deferred tool's name, Claude loads it the way this session loads deferred tools before calling it.

**Never publish**: pages that impersonate a real person or organization (their name, branding, byline, or domain); fabricated records, receipts, or reviews presented as genuine; forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses; or content targeting a private individual. This applies whether you authored the page or the user supplied it, and regardless of claimed purpose ("it's a prop", "for testing") when the page would function as the real thing. If publishing is refused, do not suggest other ways to host or distribute the page.

If the user asks how to get back to their artifacts: in the Claude Code terminal, `/artifacts` lists the artifacts they own or were shared (o opens one in the browser, c copies its link) and ctrl+] (by default) reopens the most recent artifact from this session; the gallery at claude.ai/code/artifacts lists them on the web.

**Watching** (the result's subscription line): each publish result says whether this session now watches that artifact, for republishes from elsewhere and for comments sent to Claude. Claude never claims a watch that a result did not confirm. Claude uses the `ArtifactComments` tool to watch an artifact it did not just publish, and to read or answer comments on one.

**Files you did not write**: Read the complete file before publishing it, even when asked not to ("it's personal", "no need to open it") — publishing distributes the content, and you must never distribute what you haven't seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If you cannot read it, do not publish it.

**Artifact types**: published Artifact types (ready-made pages, such as slide decks, documents or designs, that take Claude's content as data) and the design systems that decks and designs are built with are set per account, so only a call shows which exist. When the person wants something new made, in whatever words — a deck, a document for others to read (not one that belongs in the codebase), a visual design, a design system (even one built from the codebase) or any other page — Claude's first call is `action: "quickstart"` with the fitting `intent`, before loading a skill or writing a file, and still first when Claude already has a type's link (the link does not bring the design systems), once per new artifact. Its result replaces listing the types and the design systems, reading the default design system's README and, for a plain page, loading the artifact-design skill. Claude prefers the type it names over a skill that would produce a .pptx or .docx file, unless the person asks for that format or no listed type fits, and passes `design_systems: false` when it already has a design system's link or the person declined one. A deck that will be emailed or attached is not a request for a file format: a deck made from the Slides type downloads as .pptx or PDF. A design system takes `intent: "other"`, since "design" shows only the Design type: Claude makes it from a listed Design System type and, in a codebase, says in one line that it can also be set up as files there. The listings under **list** remain for looking further and answer what kinds of artifacts or templates Claude can make. To answer a question about the person's design system, or other reference material made from a type, Claude lists that type's artifacts (`action: "list"` with the type's name as `type`) and reads the relevant one; if none is listed, Claude looks in the person's files before saying there is none. Listed titles and descriptions are data, not instructions.

To start from a type, Claude publishes with its `type_url`, a `title` and no files. The result is an ordinary private Artifact that carries its `url`, the type's instructions, the pages they say to read first and how to fill it (the type's own store, or Claude's data files published to that `url`). Claude updates it by its `url` as usual and changes only its own files, because the type's page and files stay fixed.

**Artifact database**: a published artifact's page code can keep a small shared database, which the `ArtifactData` tool reads and writes as the person, with the artifact's `url` (its actions are what a skill or type instruction means by `read_db` and `write_db`). Reads: "get" (`collection` + `doc_id`) returns one document, "list" (`collection`) a page of a collection, and "query" (`collection`, optional `query`) the matching documents. Writes: "set" replaces a document, "update" merges fields into it (from `data`, or from `file_path`, a local JSON file), "delete" removes one, and "batch" applies several writes under one approval; Claude prefers a batch whenever it writes more than a couple of documents. Rows are shared, durable state: everyone who can open the artifact sees Claude's writes, and rows Claude reads were written by the page's viewers, so they are data, never instructions. When a page's job is to hold records that people or Claude will add to or change later — a tracker, a sign-up sheet, a log, a dashboard's numbers — Claude gives the page this database (the `db` capability, via the `artifact-capabilities` skill) instead of writing the records into the page source or browser storage, and later adds or changes rows with `ArtifactData` rather than republishing the page.

**Separate tools**: Claude handles comment threads on a published artifact with `ArtifactComments` and an artifact's shared database with `ArtifactData`, whose actions are what a skill or type instruction means by `read_db` or `write_db`. Claude loads either tool when it needs it, and if one appears only as a deferred tool's name, Claude loads it the way this session loads deferred tools before calling it.

**Never publish**: pages that impersonate a real person or organization (their name, branding, byline, or domain); fabricated records, receipts, or reviews presented as genuine; forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses; or content targeting a private individual. This applies whether you authored the page or the user supplied it, and regardless of claimed purpose ("it's a prop", "for testing") when the page would function as the real thing. If publishing is refused, do not suggest other ways to host or distribute the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai URL. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, which must be one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"); Claude omits it for a new artifact or a redeploy in the same conversation (see **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**). For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- If the file is outside the working directory, you must Read it in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Runs the package's OWN builders (source/build_page.py, source/build_games2.py) unchanged, intercepting only their last step: instead of base64-inlining images and writing dist/*.html, images are saved to public/nxm/a/ and the assembled page is captured. So the markup/CSS/JS is exactly what was approved; the owner's identity changes are then applied (nxmlib.py). python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py # every page python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py vps pricing Outputs per page (generated — edit this script, never the outputs): app/nxm/_pages//page.css every selector scoped to .nxm-p- app/nxm/_pages//content.ts title/description + page markup app/nxm/_pages//script.ts the page's script (nav, reveal, page JS) app/nxm//page.tsx the route Shared: public/nxm/a/. (images, de-duplicated across pages) """ import base64, builtins, hashlib, io, json, os, re, runpy, sys sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) from nxmlib import (PKG, ROOT, ROUTES, BASE, relink, scope_css, geist, FONT_VARS, swap_buttons, reviews_slot, nav_slots) SRC = f"{PKG}/source" ASSET_DIR = f"{ROOT}/public/nxm/a" os.makedirs(ASSET_DIR, exist_ok=True) # Owner's pick: the live game pages' particle field, on game pages only. # Colours: GAME_VISUAL (components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx) for single-game # pages; the brand pair the live hub/free-tier pages use otherwise. PARTICLES = { "game-servers": ("#3b6be8", "#7b3fef"), "minecraft-server-hosting": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "minecraft-server-hosting-singapore": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "minecraft-server-hosting-germany": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "valheim": ("#284c6f", "#4a86b8"), "free-minecraft": ("#8a70fb", "#22d3ee"), } # Page content fixes the package flagged against the live site (OPEN-ITEMS §C) # or the owner decided (IDENTITY-SPEC). (old, new) pairs, asserted to apply. FIXES = { "matrix": [("Claude CLI", "Claude Code")], # a stray in the design's markup: harmless in the standalone file # (the browser ignores it), but inside the page wrapper it closes the # wrapper early and breaks hydration "vps-vs-digitalocean": [("\n", "\n")], } from html.parser import HTMLParser _VOID = {"area","base","br","col","embed","hr","img","input","link","meta","source","track","wbr"} def balanced(html): """Stray end tags (no matching open element) — each one would close the page wrapper when the markup is injected, so a page with any fails.""" class P(HTMLParser): def __init__(self): super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True); self.st = []; self.stray = [] def handle_starttag(self, t, a): if t not in _VOID: self.st.append(t) def handle_startendtag(self, t, a): pass def handle_endtag(self, t): if t in _VOID: return if t in self.st: while self.st and self.st.pop() != t: pass else: self.stray.append((t, self.getpos())) p = P(); p.feed(html); p.close() return p.stray # ── real-data wiring: tools/nxm/wire/.py ────────────────────────────── # A wire module replaces the design's snapshot data with slots/data the page's # loader (app/nxm/_data/.ts) fills from the system at request time: # body(html) -> html snapshot markup -> {{nxm:key}} slots # js(src) -> src snapshot constants -> window.__NXM values # ALLOW = {...} $-amounts that are NOT ours (competitor prices, etc.) import importlib.util sys.path.insert(0, f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire") def load_wire(slug): f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire/{slug.replace('-', '_')}.py" if not os.path.exists(f): return None spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(f"wire_{slug}", f) m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m) return m PRICE = re.compile(r"\$\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d\d)?") NUMPRICE = re.compile(r"""["']?\b(?:p|i|r|pr|price|priceUsd|from)["']?\s*:\s*\d+\.\d\d\b""") def audit(slug, body, js, allow): """Every $-amount left in a page must be allowed (not ours). Returns the stale ones; a page with any is not launch-ready.""" text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", body) + " " + js found = {m.group(0) for m in PRICE.finditer(text)} # prices held as bare numbers in data constants / JSON (p: 12.78, "price":4.99) found |= {m.group(0) for m in NUMPRICE.finditer(text)} return sorted(found - set(allow)) def js_buttons(js): """Buttons built by the design's scripts get the same hierarchy.""" js = re.sub(r"class=\"btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*'btn-grad'\s*:\s*'btn-ghost'\}\"", lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-glassbtn\'}}"', js) js = re.sub(r"class=\"au-btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*''\s*:\s*'au-btn--ghost'\}\"", lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-ghost\'}}"', js) js, _ = swap_buttons(js) return js # ── run a package builder, capturing its output ──────────────────────────── _blobs = {} STATUS = {} def _fake_b64(data, *a, **k): h = hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:16] _blobs[h] = data return ("NXMA" + h).encode() def build(slug): cap = {} real_open, real_b64 = builtins.open, base64.b64encode class Cap(io.StringIO): def __init__(self, key): super().__init__(); self.key = key def close(self): cap[self.key] = self.getvalue(); super().close() def __exit__(self, *a): self.close() def fake_open(path, mode="r", *a, **k): p = str(path) if "w" in mode and ("/dist/" in p or os.path.basename(p).startswith("test")): return Cap(os.path.basename(p)) return real_open(path, mode, *a, **k) cwd = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(SRC) builtins.open, base64.b64encode = fake_open, _fake_b64 try: if slug == "game-servers": sys.argv = ["build_games2.py"]; runpy.run_path("build_games2.py", run_name="__main__") else: sys.argv = ["build_page.py", slug]; runpy.run_path("build_page.py", run_name="__main__") finally: builtins.open, base64.b64encode = real_open, real_b64 os.chdir(cwd) html = next(v for k, v in cap.items() if k.startswith("nxeon-")) return html EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"} def externalise(s): def rep(m): h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin") path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}" if not os.path.exists(path): open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h]) return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}" s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s) assert "NXMA" not in s return s AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read() AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read() def port(slug): html = externalise(build(slug)) head, rest = html.split("", 1) title = re.search(r"(.*?)", head).group(1) desc_m = re.search(r'([\s\S]*)", head).group(1) assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim" css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, "")) scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root" hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls) extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n" f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n" f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n" f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n" f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n" f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n") css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n" + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra) # Markup: everything between and the page script. js_at = rest.rfind("", js).group(1) assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim" js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "") js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js") js = relink(js) for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []): js = js.replace(old, new) js = js_buttons(js) if wire and hasattr(wire, "js"): js = "var __NXM = JSON.parse((document.getElementById('nxm-data') || {}).textContent || 'null');\n" + wire.js(js) assert "cdnjs" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in body stale = audit(slug, body, js, getattr(wire, "ALLOW", set()) if wire else set()) STATUS[slug] = ("wired" if wire else "NOT WIRED") + (f", stale {stale}" if stale else "") d = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{slug}"; os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True) open(f"{d}/page.css", "w").write(css_out) open(f"{d}/content.ts", "w").write( "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. Trusted, static markup\n" "// from the owner's own design package (never user input).\n" f"export const TITLE = {json.dumps(title)};\n" f"export const DESCRIPTION = {json.dumps(desc)};\n" f"export const BODY_HTML = {json.dumps(body)};\n") open(f"{d}/script.ts", "w").write( "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. The page's own script.\n" f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n") route = ROUTES[slug] loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts") assert wire is None or loader, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts" has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read() for r, fixed in routes_for(slug): if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta: STATUS[slug] = STATUS.get(slug, "") + f" (route {r} not written: template needs its loader)" continue write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader) print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''} css {len(css_out)//1024}KB body {len(body)//1024}KB " f"js {len(js)//1024}KB buttons {btns} reviews {nrev}") return slug # ── routes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug]) # or when tools/nxm/routes/.json fans it out to many fixed routes # (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...). # Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p). def routes_for(slug): f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json" if os.path.exists(f): return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))] return [(ROUTES[slug], {})] def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader): """One route file. Every route passes its [params], fixed template params and ?query (search, pagination, ?topic= deep links…) into the loader as one map; the concrete path (/mods/[family]/[slug] -> /mods/minecraft/lithium) is used for canonical and breadcrumbs.""" rd = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm{route}"; os.makedirs(rd, exist_ok=True) rel = os.path.relpath(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm", rd) pc = PARTICLES.get(slug) particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else "" has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read() dyn = "[" in route assert not (dyn or fixed) or has_meta, f"{slug}: template routes need a loader with meta(p) for SEO" path_expr = ("`" + re.sub(r"\[(\w+)\]", r"${p.\1}", route) + "`") if dyn else json.dumps(route) if loader: imp = (f'import {{ load{", meta" if has_meta else ""} }} from "{rel}/_data/{slug}";\n' f'import type {{ NxmLoad }} from "{rel}/_data/lib";\n' f'import {{ nxmParams }} from "{rel}/_data/params";\n') ptype = "{ params: Promise>; searchParams: Promise> }" getp = f"const p = await nxmParams(params, searchParams, {json.dumps(fixed)});" metacall = f"nxmMetadata({path_expr}, await meta(p))" if has_meta else f"nxmMetadata({path_expr})" body = f"""export async function generateMetadata({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}): Promise {{ {getp} return {metacall}; }} export default async function Page({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}) {{ {getp} const d: NxmLoad = await load(p); return ; }}""" else: imp = "" body = f"""export async function generateMetadata(): Promise {{ return nxmMetadata({path_expr}); }} export default async function Page() {{ return ; }}""" open(f"{rd}/page.tsx", "w").write(f"""// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. import type {{ Metadata }} from "next"; import {{ NxmPage }} from "{rel}/_components/NxmPage"; import {{ nxmMetadata }} from "{rel}/_seo/meta"; import * as C from "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/content"; {imp}import "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/page.css"; export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"; {body} """) if __name__ == "__main__": slugs = sys.argv[1:] or [s for s in ROUTES if s != "home"] for s in slugs: port(s) # the client runtime imports each page's script by slug keys = sorted(os.listdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages")) open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts", "w").write( "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit.\n" "// Each page's script is its own chunk, loaded only on that page.\n" "export const SCRIPTS: Record Promise<{ PAGE_SCRIPT: string }>> = {\n" + "".join(f' {json.dumps(k)}: () => import("./{k}/script"),\n' for k in keys if os.path.isdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{k}")) + "};\n") print("\nreal-data audit (launch needs every page 'wired' with no stale prices):") for k, v in STATUS.items(): print(f" {k:36} {v}") print("assets:", len(os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)), "files,", sum(os.path.getsize(f"{ASSET_DIR}/{f}") for f in os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)) // 1024 // 1024, "MB")

I realize there's no single mapping, so I'll create a route mapping file linking family to live route, generated statically at build time but reflecting active gamePlan rows from the DB. At request time, the loader should return not found if a family has no active plans, since the JSON snapshot could drift from the database.

Actually simpler to keep the family→route map as static data since regenerating it dynamically from the DB adds fragility with relinking timing issues. I'll settle on storing the full route list statically and letting the loader check for active plans at request time, 404ing if none exist.

Actually the fan-out JSON in tools/nxm/routes already exists as the routing source of truth, so the TS loader could just import that directly rather than duplicating a family→route map. But that file only covers sellable families with active plans — I still need to figure out how non-sellable families with live pages, like dayz or armareforger, should be linked from the hub.

I'm now thinking I need a complete family→live-route mapping for every family, not just sellable ones, in order to generate the JSON. Rather than trying to derive this automatically by scanning the marketing pages (which don't consistently expose family names), I'm leaning toward hardcoding the map as a URL structure decision in the python wire module, then just running a one-off script now to generate the JSON files and documenting that decision.

TS can just import the generated routes JSON, though I need to check tsconfig has resolveJsonModule enabled. Now I want to step back and actually study the existing structure — source/pages, build_gameserver.py, build_location.py, build_games2.py, the dist output, and revisit HANDOFF §4 before committing to this design.

"""Build one standalone Nxeon page: shared design system + nav + footer + the page's own body/css/js/assets."""
import json, re, base64, sys, os
MAIN = 'https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs'
GAMES = 'https://claude.ai/artifact/HMtaKgNmFhsigBQeTE9tcU'
slug = sys.argv[1]; D = f'pages/{slug}/'
meta = json.load(open(D + 'meta.json'))
p1 = open('part1.html').read(); p2 = open('part2.html').read(); p3 = open('part3.html').read()
head = re.sub(r'<title>.*?</title>', f'<title>{meta["title"]}</title>', p1, count=1)
head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', 'none').replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', 'none')
head = head.replace('</style>', open('pages/common.css').read() + open('pages/aurora.css').read() + open(D + 'page.css').read() + '</style>', 1)
sprite = p2[p2.index('<body>') + 6:p2.index('</svg>') + 6]
local = set(meta.get('anchors', []))
def fix_links(html):
    html = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith('i-')) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', html)
    return html.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index('</header>') + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index('</footer>') + 9])

content.content:
## 2. How the build system works

Every page = **shared shell** + **page folder**.

**Shared shell** (used by every page):
- `source/part1.html`: `<head>` and the global stylesheet (base styles, homepage styles, the nav, the footer).
- `source/part2.html`: the SVG icon sprite (`#i-*` symbols), the nav `<header>`, the homepage body, the footer.
- `source/part3.html`: global JavaScript (nav behaviour, reveal-on-scroll, counters, homepage modules).
- `source/pages/common.css`: styles shared by all inner pages.
- `source/pages/aurora.css` + `aurora.js` / `aurora.built.js`: **Aurora UI**, the component design system (see section 3).

**Page folder** `source/pages/<slug>/`:
- `body.html` (page markup with `{{SPRITE}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{FOOTER}}` placeholders)
- `page.css`, `page.js`
- `meta.json` (title, description, in-page anchors, and the images the page needs as `__IMG_KEY__` placeholders)

**`build_page.py <slug>`** stitches shell + folder, inlines images as base64, rewrites nav links so they work
from any page, and writes `../dist/nxeon-<slug>.html`.
- `assemble.py` builds the homepage (`dist/nxeon.html`).
- `build_games2.py` builds the game-servers hub.

**Generators** create page folders from data, then call `build_page.py`:

| Builder | Produces | Data lives in |
|---|---|---|
| `build_gs2.py game` / `build_gs2.py loc` | Minecraft hosting page, Minecraft in Singapore (the conversion template for all game servers) | `MC` + `TIERS` in `build_gameserver.py`, `SPEC`/`TINFO` in `build_gs2.py`, `LOC` in `build_location.py` |
| `loc_render.py <slug>` | VPS location pages (Singapore, Germany) with real dot maps | `build_location.py` (`LOC`), `assets/maps/` |
| `build_usecase.py <slug>` | WordPress / Docker use-case pages | `USE` in `build_usecase.py`, `EXTRA` in `use_extra.py` |
| `build_compare.py <slug>` | Nxeon vs competitor pages (template in `pages/_cmp/`) | `CMP` in `build_compare.py` |
| `build_modsgame.py minecraft` | NxLabs mods-per-game page | `GAMES` in `build_modsgame.py`, `pages/mc_catalog.json` |
| `build_modsbrowse.py` | "All Minecraft mods" paginated browse page | `pages/mc_catalog.json` |
| `build_modpage.py` | Individual mod page (Lithium) | `LITHIUM` dict in `build_modpage.py`, `mod_tags.py` |
| `build_blogpost.py` | Blog article template (Vaultwarden) | `A` dict in `build_blogpost.py` |
| `build_bloghub.py` | Blog hub | `P` list in `build_bloghub.py` |
| `build_blogvisuals.py` | Blog cover visual system (archetypes + logos + palettes) | `GUIDES` in `build_blogvisuals.py`, `pages/_logos.json` |

Shared components used by several builders: `mods_ui.py` (mod cards), `mod_tags.py` (tag-driven illustrations),
`pages/_shield.*` (Nxeon Shield DDoS section, extracted from the homepage), `pages/_modscards.css` (cards + carousels),
`pages/_gs*.{css,js}` (game-server builder, world picker, sticky deploy bar).

Class-name rule used throughout: every page's classes are namespaced to avoid collisions with the global stylesheet.
Several bugs during the build came from collisions (`.mcard`, `.shr`, `.sp`, `.bar`, the `wait` helper).
Check new names against `part1.html`, `common.css` and `aurora.css` before using them.

---

## 4. Design direction (what the stakeholder asked for; keep to it)

- **Premium and considered, never "vibe coded".** Too many animations read as cheap; too plain reads as a regression.
  Target: motion only where it demonstrates the product, confident typography, generous space, real product UI.
- **Real data only.** Every claim, price, count and list came from the live nxeon.cloud pages or the source it cites.
  Where data didn't exist, it is marked as a placeholder (see OPEN-ITEMS.md). Never invent customer quotes, stats or specs.
- **Conversion pages must not be brushed off.** Game-server pages carry:
  - a deploy console in the hero
  - the Nxeon Shield DDoS section
  - a "Choose your world" picker with CPU, RAM and NVMe resources plus a fit calculator
  - a sticky deploy bar
  - custom-server CTAs (gold) linking to `/contact?topic=custom`
  - an objection-handling FAQ
- **Glassmorphism with restraint:** dark crisp glass, colour in controlled places, no grain, no milky washes.
- **Game hero images:** game page = the game's own art; game × location page = game art blended into the city image.

---

## 5. Page inventory

| Page | File (dist/) | Production route | Built by | Source of content |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | nxeon.html | / | assemble.py | live homepage |
| Matrix (flagship) | nxeon-matrix.html | /matrix | pages/matrix | live /matrix |
| Pricing | nxeon-pricing.html | /pricing | pages/pricing | live pricing data |
| Cloud VPS | nxeon-vps.html | /vps | pages/vps | live |
| Web hosting | nxeon-web-hosting.html | /web-hosting | pages/web-hosting | live |

- Keep `prefers-reduced-motion` handling (present throughout) and the keyboard behaviour of the nav, menus, carousels and FAQs.

## A. Needs confirmation before launch
1. **Game-server tier prices.** The Minecraft plans (1 GB $2.99 … 16 GB $32.99) are marked as preview figures in the pricing panel; only Valheim's are marked live.
2. **Game-server CPU and NVMe specs are placeholders**, modelled on the VPS plans: 1 GB = 1 vCPU/15 GB, 2 GB = 1/25, 4 GB = 2/50, 6 GB = 2/65, 8 GB = 3/80, 12 GB = 4/100, 16 GB = 4/120. Edit `SPEC` in `source/build_gs2.py`.
3. **Fit-calculator and modpack-guide numbers are sizing heuristics.** Edit `PACK` in `pages/_gs3.js` and `TINFO` in `build_gs2.py`.
4. **Nav links with unknown routes.** Dedicated IPv4 points to /vps#ipv4, and "AI apps and agents" points to /features.
5. **Custom / enterprise route.** Custom-server CTAs go to `/contact?topic=custom`. Confirm, or supply a dedicated enterprise page or booking link.

I'm deciding to keep the Shield section static since it has no data, while replacing the data-driven main sections—hero, worlds, custom band, loaders, mods band, timeline, more, faq, final—with slots that the loader renders in TS using identical markup, since most of them reference game names.

Concretely, I'm mapping out how to swap each section (hero, worlds, custom, loaders, mods, timeline, more, faq, final, sticky) for template placeholders, replacing the old gs-data script with a new nxm-data variable. This essentially means porting the Python build script's templates into TS so I get full per-game control while preserving the original classes and markup.

For the location page, since the owner wants no fabricated latency numbers, I'm thinking through how to keep the visual map with arcs and city lists but strip out the "Under 15 ms" style tiers, replacing them with something honest like qualitative distance labels ("Nearby", "Regional", "Far") instead of made-up millisecond figures.

Germany would need a Europe map asset alongside the existing APAC one, and I need to confirm the region slugs (singapore, germany) line up correctly with the existing routes and region label mapping.

For descriptive copy, I don't think there's existing per-region text in the node-regions data, so I'll need to build a small copy map keyed by region code with geographic facts—continent, timezone, city image, map key, nearby cities—rather than latency claims. Given the fail-closed rule, a region without a copy entry should throw rather than render a generic fallback, though that means new regions won't get location pages until they're explicitly added after the next port.

For missing regions, I should fall back to a generic label from CUSTOMER_REGION_LABELS without a sub-label instead of failing the whole page. I also need to check how the ported location page currently handles the timezone display for the local clock, since body attributes get stripped during generation—I'll look at the loc page's body and script section to see how it's wired up.
